threads.body:
It looks like `numpy.fft` may be patched to `mkl_fft` when NumPy is installed from Intel channels (software.repos.intel.com/python/conda or gold)
 ```
$ python -c "import numpy as np; print(np.fft.fftn.__module__)"
mkl_fft.interfaces._numpy_fft
```
This means the tests may not always use the real `numpy.fft` implementation as the reference, contrary to the docstring on 35 line

Could we use the NumPy implementation directly instead? Something like this?
```
from numpy.fft import _pocketfft as npfft
```
and use npfft.* for the reference calls
threads.author: vlad-perevezentsev

threads.body:
This function almost exactly replicates the logic in `_cook_nd_args`
It looks like we can reuse it
Something like this
```
def _nd_fwd_scale(x, s, axes, norm, invreal=False):
    """Forward scale of an N-D transform, normalized over the transformed axes.

    ``_compute_fwd_scale`` falls back to the full array shape when ``s`` is
    None, which over-normalizes a subset-of-axes transform; for c2r the basis
    is the output length ``2 * (n - 1)``. Both are exactly what
    ``_cook_nd_args`` already resolves for the transform itself.
    """
    _check_norm(norm)
    if norm in (None, "backward"):
        return 1.0
    if s is None:
        s, _ = _cook_nd_args(x, s, axes, invreal=invreal)
    return _compute_fwd_scale(norm, s, x.shape)
```

`return _compute_fwd_scale(norm, s, x.shape)` will also help reduce the code in the fft functions 
```
fsc = _nd_fwd_scale(x, s, axes, norm)

#instead of 

ss = _compute_nd_scale_shape(x, s, axes, norm)
fsc = _compute_fwd_scale(norm, ss, x.shape)
`
